publication.body:
Closes #1082

Add provider-neutral Bedrock Converse support and migrate two unreliable residents to current Bedrock models while keeping agent identity independent from model selection.
publication.title: Adopt Bedrock Converse for durable resident bindings

plan.acceptance: Merged provider-neutral lifecycle #855, provider-definition work #876, resident monitoring #854, and typed failure projection #1079.

Issue #1082; adl-provider-core Bedrock adapter and profiles; Runtime resident admission, identity continuity, conversation and provider-health surfaces; current Agent Logic Bedrock model authorization; Axioma Polis welcome package.
adl-provider-core/src/http_family.rs and focused tests; provider registry/profile surfaces required for Converse; adl-runtime-kernel resident binding and continuity surfaces; docs/provider/inference-profiles.md and docs/runtime/RESIDENT_PROVIDER_MONITORING.md; issue-scoped live configuration/proof inputs outside tracked main.

Provider-neutral Bedrock Converse request/response handling; bounded Kimi K2.5 and Nemotron Super 3 120B definitions; two durable model-independent residents; explicit continuity migration from legacy model-derived identities; welcome-package, conversation, A2A, health and Observatory proof.

Focused provider-core Converse request, response, failure and cancellation tests; Runtime identity/model-rebind continuity and readiness tests; formatting and strict Clippy for touched crates; independent exact-head review; bounded live conversations and A2A exchanges under a documented cost ceiling with no retry after ambiguous outcomes.
Agent names and identities are independent of provider/model bindings; model swaps do not rename agents or reset continuity; Bedrock Converse supports the exact qualified Kimi and Nemotron models without Nova payloads; legacy identity history migrates explicitly; welcome package, operator conversation, governed A2A, provider health and Observatory readiness pass; no recurring paid probes.

Do not name new residents after providers or models, silently discard legacy continuity, widen to every Bedrock catalog model, migrate healthy DeepSeek, expose AWS identity or credentials, retry ambiguous live calls, or introduce recurring inference.
